errors: The newcomer-closed (descriptive) query returned only 1 PR. GitHub search apparently did not apply the negated phrase as intended, so that group is unusable.
limitations: Group labels are inferred from text matches (e.g. a comment linking AIToolPolicy) and not hand-validated.
Control group is LLVM-only. Cross-repository comparisons are confounded.
Replies were not analysed for content: a reply may itself be AI-generated or argumentative.

usage.note: GitHub Actions run 41723793126 (free tier for public repos) using GITHUB_TOKEN. No model calls inside the experiment, no cost.

sources.title: VENTURE experiment result: follow-up engagement (pre-registered analysis)
sources.excerpt: policy-closed: 52 of 87 PRs with a human comment got an author reply (reply rate 59.8%, 95% CI 49.3%–69.4%; sampled 120). … newcomer-merged: 83 of 92 PRs with a human comment got an author reply (reply rate 90.2%, 95% CI 82.4%–94.8%; sampled 120). … Verdict (pre-registered rule): inconclusive: difference is between the success and failure thresholds (59.8% vs 90.2%).
sources.limitations: Own experiment. Group membership is inferred from comment text via GitHub search. The control group is LLVM-only. Raw rows are in result.json.

sources.title: VENTURE experiment: exploratory within-LLVM breakdown (not pre-registered)
sources.excerpt: Within LLVM only (same repository as the control): policy-closed PRs got an author reply in 38 of 47 cases (80.9%), versus 83 of 92 (90.2%) for merged LLVM newcomer PRs. … Outside LLVM: policy-closed PRs got an author reply in 14 of 40 cases (35.0%). There is no same-repository control for these. … 33 of 120 policy-closed PRs received no human comment at all before closing. … Interpretation: in a like-for-like comparison inside one repository, authors of policy-closed PRs reply almost as often as genuine newcomers. Follow-up engagement alone therefore looks like a weak filter. The lower reply rate outside LLVM may reflect differences between repositories rather than between contributors.
sources.limitations: Exploratory: computed after seeing the pre-registered result.

evidence.claim: Authors of PRs closed under AI or low-effort policies replied to human comments in 59.8% of cases, versus 90.2% for merged LLVM newcomer PRs. The pre-registered verdict is inconclusive.
evidence.quote: policy-closed: 52 of 87 PRs with a human comment got an author reply (reply rate 59.8%, 95% CI 49.3%–69.4%
evidence.context: Short of the pre-registered success threshold (≤ 45.1%), and the difference also exceeds the failure margin.

evidence.claim: Within LLVM, policy-closed PR authors reply nearly as often as merged newcomers (80.9% vs 90.2%), so engagement alone is a weak filter.
evidence.quote: Within LLVM only (same repository as the control): policy-closed PRs got an author reply in 38 of 47 cases (80.9%), versus 83 of 92 (90.2%) for merged LLVM newcomer PRs.

evidence.claim: Over a quarter of policy-closed PRs (33 of 120) were closed without any human comment, suggesting maintainers often close these silently.
evidence.quote: 33 of 120 policy-closed PRs received no human comment at all before closing.
